title: 160 killed in deadly Nepal deluge; at least 133 Indians among 844 missing
content: Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.

title: SC judge complains against Raj acting CJ; CJI Surya Kant seeks response
content: ustice Mehta, who also hails from Rajasthan HC, has accused Justice Sharma of lacking in leadership qualities and alleged there was maladministration and malpractice on both judicial and administrative sides of HC. CJI Kant told TOI that the matter can be resolved only as per the established mechanism. “The Supreme Court cannot allow individual complaints concerning judges to be determined through competing claims in the media,” he said.

title: Nepal floods: MEA issues helpline numbers as over 100 Indians go missing
content: The Embassy of India in Kathmandu has issued emergency helpline numbers for assistance and information regarding Indian nationals affected by the flash floods in Nepal. Those seeking assistance can contact +977 985 131 6807 or +977 970 910 7500, the MEA said. Of the 291 foreign nationals reported missing, others include citizens of Australia, the Netherlands, the United States, Malaysia, the United Kingdom and South Africa.

title: ‘Absolute shame’: DDCA draws flak amid Dev Chaudhary row
content: Dev Chaudhary’s selection by New Delhi Tigers has raised questions over the DPL’s rule allowing franchises to pick three players outside the auction. Chaudhary played two matches despite limited known credentials, prompting criticism from DDCA Apex Council member Shyam Sharma. DDCA secretary Ashok Sharma said the rule will be reviewed after the tournament amid concerns over recommendations and selection practices.

title: Ahead of Xi Jinping’s visit, India & China announce 8-point consensus
content: These included advancing consultations for an “early and substantial harvest” of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing the ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, and expanding trans-border trade and river cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the talks.

title: In 1984, NASA sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
content: In 1984, NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery took thousands of honeybees into space, marking a unique experiment in microgravity. These resilient insects adapted quickly to their extraterrestrial surroundings, building about 200 centimeters of honeycomb in just seven days. Researchers studied the differences in the bees' construction, noting significant variations in cell size and wall thickness between their cosmic creations and those made on Earth.

title: 3 lakh tonnes of refined sugar to enter market
content: Govt had allowed duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar and also allowed the processors to sell some refined sugar, which was meant for export only, in the domestic market. Officials and industry insiders said at least 3 lakh tonnes of processed sugar could come into the market quickly. The subsequent import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will help tide over any supply issue. Meanwhile, the ex-mill price of sugar has gone down by 20% in the past 10 days.

title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs
content: Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.  In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June.

title: Anthropic tells SF staff to WFH over security guard strike threat that union denies
content: Anthropic asked employees at its San Francisco offices to work from home on Monday and Tuesday after security contractor Allied Universal warned of a possible strike by its guards. The SEIU, which represents those workers, says it has called no strike authorisation vote and issued no strike threat this week. The union has been negotiating with California security firms over wages and healthcare since April.

title: Nepal flood: For centuries, flood-hit corridor was key route of Himalayan trade
content: Long before trucks climbed Bhote Koshi valley, mule caravans carried rice and other grain from Nepal north to Gyirong, where traders exchanged them for Tibetan salt and wool. Salt, highly valued in Nepal’s middle hills, travelled farther south towards India. Newar merchant communities also settled in Tibetan trading towns. Nepalese troops later used the route during invasions of Tibet in 1788 and 1791 before Chinese and Tibetan forces counter-attacked in 1792.

title: New pigment-free coating stays 6C cooler than surrounding air in desert sun
content: Columbia Engineering researchers developed a porous polymer coating that can cool surfaces below the surrounding air temperature without using electricity. The coating replaces conventional white pigments with nano-to-microscale air voids that reflect sunlight and release heat towards the sky. Tests showed the surface stayed about 6°C below ambient temperature in Arizona and 3°C below it in Bangladesh.

title: Savannah audits 39,000 Flock searches; 6 employees fired, 4 arrested
content: Four former Savannah Police Department employees have been arrested over alleged misuse of the Flock Safety license plate reader system. The arrests followed an internal audit of 39,000 searches, which flagged 127 for review and found 34 were unjustified. Six employees were fired, while the Georgia Bureau of Investigation continues to investigate the case.

title: ‘Shocked’ by hacks, Bill Gates wants to meet China’s Xi Jinping
content: Bill Gates is set to engage with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this year, discussing the pressing need for international collaboration to manage the risks associated with artificial intelligence. Concerned by recent AI-related security incidents, Gates suggests that if the U.S. takes the lead, China may follow in restricting hazardous AI models. He pushes for a global regulatory framework akin to those in nuclear and aviation sectors.

title: UN panel report on minorities is politically motivated: Govt
content: UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination had “highlighted” in a report the increase in law enforcement operations targeting “Rohingya, Bengali-speaking Muslims, migrants and asylum-seekers, particularly following the 2017 home affairs order and the April 2025 Pahalgam attack in Kashmir”. Ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “India rejects any politically motivated, highly malicious references in the report with all the contempt that it deserves.”

title: As obesity rises, Supreme Court puts govt on notice over junk food labels
content: The order, in response to a PIL filed by NGO ‘3S and Our HEALTH Society’ which moved SC through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi, comes as govt has seemed reluctant to implement front-of-pack warning labels on junk food. SC said food with high salt, sugar, saturated fat and calories could lead to health risks and clearer nutrition information must be displayed to help to make healthier choices.

title: Low beam by default: Centre to tighten headlamp norms
content: The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, along with the mandatory provision for buses and other heavy vehicles to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules. Amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made because efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.

title: 'Someone I watched growing up': Zane Maloney joins Oliver Rowland at Nissan
content: Zane Maloney grew up watching Oliver Rowland win races. Now, the young Barbadian will race alongside the Formula E World Champion as his Nissan teammate. The 22-year-old will join the Japanese team for the 2026/27 Formula E season and sees it as a big step in his career. Maloney says he is also excited about the chance to learn from Rowland.

title: At 6, Novak Djokovic met a coach who changed his life forever at tennis camp
content: At a tennis camp, Jelena Genčić identified young Novak Djokovic's remarkable concentration and innate talent. Her insight extended far beyond enhancing his tennis abilities; she offered vital mentorship during his difficult upbringing. Genčić's pivotal role included assisting Djokovic's transition to Germany for enriched training and prospects, ultimately laying the groundwork for his ascent to tennis stardom.

title: Everything we know about Ananta: Release date, gameplay, platforms and more
content: Set to launch globally on January 15, 2027, Ananta, previously known as Project Mugen, promises an engaging free-to-play open-world RPG experience for PlayStation 5 and PC users. Players will enjoy dynamic gameplay featuring thrilling gunfights, adrenaline-pumping car chases, and innovative web-slinging mechanics. Character and attire customization will be expansive, allowing players to express their unique styles through cosmetic purchases instead of relying on a gacha mechanism.

title: Beyond fish in Ayodhya row: Why Nishad vote matters in UP 2027 battle
content: A fish controversy in Uttar Pradesh has highlighted the Nishad community's political significance.  This community's vote has shifted loyalties and remains a key factor for parties.  The BJP seeks to retain its OBC coalition while opposition parties try to gain support.  Nishad leaders have historical ties to epic narratives and social justice movements.  The 2027 elections will test alliances and demands for representation and livelihoods.

title: Wireless communication picked up; search operation launched in J&K's Samba
content: “Terrorists often switch off such communication devices after contacting their handlers across the border,” said a source, adding that Iridium sets can be used on smartphones through the “Iridium GO!” mobile application, which creates a local Wi-Fi network that an iOS or Android phone can connect to. The operation continued until late Tuesday, but no satellite set or other suspicious material was found.

title: 5.2 kg heroin seized in Jammu, NCB busts Pakistan network; 3 held
content: “Preliminary investigation led NCB to another resident of Baramulla, the suspected mastermind. He was traced and arrested in Leh on Aug 24. The seized drug, suspected to have been smuggled from Pakistan, entered India through the Uri border sector,” the NCB official said. “The probe will identify cross-border suppliers, financial links, transporters, local associates, and the intended distribution network,” the spokesperson added.

title: 6 dead, 3 hurt as vehicle falls into gorge in J&K’s Poonch
content: The accident occurred around 5.30pm. Officials suspected the driver had lost control of the vehicle, which rolled into the gorge, killing six occupants — Mohd Shafiq (32), Nazakat Hussain (34), Sheraz Ahmed (30), Musarat Naz (19), Mohd Fareed (21), and Zulfat Bi (25) — on the spot, police said. Upon receiving information, cops reached the spot and launched a rescue operation with the help of locals.

title: ‘I’m retired bro’: Gukesh’s cheeky reply to troll gets unexpected twist
content: World champion D Gukesh shared a funny exchange with an online troll who initially told him to retire. After Gukesh jokingly replied, “Sorry I’m retired bro” when asked for a chess match, the user revealed it was a dare from friends. Gukesh posted the exchange with “Haters are fun bro” amid scrutiny over his recent form.

title: Raids & kidnapping drills: How Chinese students are prepping for Trump's US
content: Chinese students now receive survival training before attending American universities.  This preparation addresses perceived immigration system unpredictability and potential hostility.  New immigration rules and heightened scrutiny create significant anxiety for families.  Students must now navigate admission, visa, and legal status concerns.  This reflects a shift from academic focus to survival preparation for studying abroad.

title: Detained by ICE, US Green Card holder from Andhra Pradesh gets bail
content: Venkata Narasamamba Vasamsetty, an Indian-origin woman and legal permanent resident for almost thirty years, recently received bail from a federal court in Georgia. Her detention by Immigration and Customs Enforcement occurred despite her immigration case being dismissed, raising family concerns about unequal treatment and the harsh conditions she faced. While the bail decision brings some respite, ongoing worries regarding her immigration status remain.

title: PM Balen Shah appeals for unity after monster floods batter Nepal; Bihar, UP on high alert
content: A massive flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district has caused widespread damage and claimed seventeen lives. Over one hundred Indian nationals are reported missing after the sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River. Many missing individuals are believed to be pilgrims traveling to Tibet for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. Rescue operations are underway with helicopters and drones searching for the missing people.

title: Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan shot dead in UP just 2 hours after he shared video
content: Tragedy struck as Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan was shot dead by unidentified gunmen outside a gym in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh, on Wednesday evening. Despite prompt medical attention, he was pronounced dead at the hospital shortly thereafter. Famous for his songs and social media influence, Balyan was reportedly gearing up for local elections. Authorities are actively investigating the incident and examining CCTV footage for leads.

title: Gold may hit Rs 15 lakh? Billionaire investor sees 10-fold rise as ‘inevitable’
content: Gold prices have corrected in the last few months from their historic highs after rising meteorically the whole of 2025. This led many to question whether the bull run in the precious metal is over.

title: 'Give supporters reasons to stay': Ramiz Raja warns Pakistan

Former captain Ramiz Raja noted an alarming rift between the players and supporters. With captain Babar Azam possibly returning, the team hopes to revitalize their batting order. England, fresh off their success, aims to assert dominance in the forthcoming Test at Lord's, while Pakistan desperately seeks a win to equalize the series.

title: Nepal floods: Terrifying videos show homes, buildings and bridges swallowed by raging waters

With river currents surging unexpectedly, the fate of many remains uncertain, as reports indicate that over a hundred Indians and thirty-seven NRIs are unaccounted for. Local authorities have declared high alerts, strongly encouraging residents to seek refuge in safer areas.

Authorities are monitoring trends and hospital readiness to manage patient care effectively.

After winning national and international medals, Kundu missed the Paris Olympics due to injury but made a remarkable comeback, securing his place for the Commonwealth and Asian Games.

title: Parandur airport scrapped: What happens to the land now?
content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has formally scrapped the proposed ₹27,400-crore Parandur greenfield airport project, bringing an end to years of protests by villagers and farmers. But the decision has triggered a new question: what happens to the thousands of acres of land that were already acquired for the project?

Can the government return the land to original owners? What does the Land Acquisition Act say? And what options does Tamil Nadu have now that the project has been shelved?

In this explainer, we break down the legal provisions, the status of acquired land, previous examples of land return in Tamil Nadu, and what the future could hold for Parandur and its residents.

title: 'Like a bomb exploded': How a 2,000-ft wide glacier triggered deadly Nepal floods
content: flash floods may have been triggered by a massive chunk of glacier breaking away high in the mountains and crashing into a river valley below . a glacier about 2,000 feet wide snapped off almost cleanly and fell from an altitude of around 17,000 feet . the block dropped nearly 4,000 feet before reaching the valley floor .

title: 2015 earthquake, 2026 floods: Why Nepal is so susceptible to natural disasters
content: flash floods sweeping through communities along the Bhote Koshi and other rivers, killing dozens and leaving hundreds missing . the disaster has devastated settlements, roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure in northern Nepal, while a mudslide in Tibet has also caused deaths . officials have warned people to stay away from the banks of the rivers while helicopters have been deployed to rescue people stranded by floodwaters .
